classification.difficultyReason: Convert bracket intervals into number-line graphs with appropriate endpoints and rays.

content.prompt: Graph these intervals on the real number line.

answer.short: Closed endpoint at $3$; ray to the right.
answer.worked: The square bracket includes $3$. Draw a closed circle at $3$ and a ray to the right.

solutionDiagrams.code:
% mathsmap-diagram-colours {"version":1,"kind":"graph","base":[],"semantic":[],"reference":"Exercise 2A 5a, teacher PDF page 5"}
\begin{tikzpicture}[x=0.52cm,y=0.6cm]\special{dvisvgm:raw <metadata data-graph-strokes="1"/>}\draw[->,line width=0.5pt] (-6,0)--(6.2,0) node[right] {$x$};\foreach \x in {-5,...,5}{\draw[line width=0.4pt] (\x,-.08)--(\x,.08);\node[below] at (\x,-.1){\special{dvisvgm:raw <g data-graph-text="tick">}$\x$\special{dvisvgm:raw </g>}};}\draw[->,line width=0.8pt] (3,.65)--(6,.65);\fill (3,.65) circle (2pt);\end{tikzpicture}

spec.description: Number line with a raised interval ray; the template cannot express interval rays.

answer.short: Open endpoint at $1$; ray to the left.
answer.worked: The round bracket excludes $1$. Draw an open circle at $1$ and a ray to the left.

answer.short: Closed endpoint at $-5$, open endpoint at $5$; join them.
answer.worked: Include $-5$ with a closed circle, exclude $5$ with an open circle, and join the endpoints.
